s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Rash is pruritic and has been present for 3 months
Patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus

per_call: Panniculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and presents with a pruritic rash and firm, red-brown plaques, which are consistent with scleromyxedema

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and presents with firm, red-brown plaques, which are consistent with morphea

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with a pruritic rash and firm, red-brown plaques, and has a history of systemic sclerosis, which are consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis

shortlist.label: Scleredema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with a pruritic rash and firm, red-brown plaques, which are consistent with scleredema

shortlist.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and presents with firm, red-brown plaques, which are consistent with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, along with the histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers and homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles, is consistent with scleromyxedema. The absence of skin tightening in the affected areas and the lack of preceding triggers or trauma also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with skin tightening and sclerosis, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic fasciitis is characterized by rapid progression of skin thickening and inflammation, which is not consistent with this patient's 3-month history of a pruritic rash.

rejected.label: Scleredema
rejected.why: Scleredema is typically associated with diabetes or infections, which are not present in this patient's history.

rejected.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
rejected.why: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis is associated with renal failure and exposure to gadolinium-based contrast agents, which are not mentioned in the patient's history.
